section.title: Purpose
section.para: This document states the system requirements (SRQs) of the JetOS hypervisor. The high level requirements of the functions of the hypervisor, which are written in the headers of the functions and published in the function documentation (docs/hypervisor.pdf and docs/shared.pdf), are traced to the requirements of this document.

section.title: Scope: what the hypervisor is
section.para: The hypervisor (hypervisor/) is the software that runs at the highest privilege level of a computer and shares it between virtual machines (VMs), each of which runs one JetOS image. It supports x86_64 processors with AMD SVM and arm64 processors with EL2. Its configuration (the VMs, their images, memory, processors and serial ports) is fixed when the hypervisor is built.

The hypervisor consists of its core (hypervisor/core), the CPU support packages of the two architectures (hypervisor/csps), the board support packages, which hold the devices of the board and the virtual devices of the VMs (hypervisor/bsps), and the library and the headers that it shares with the JetOS kernel (common/ and include/), as they are used by the hypervisor.
JetOS itself (the kernel and the board support packages) is not in the scope of this document: its requirements are in the document JetOS System Requirements.

section.title: Conventions
section.para: A requirement has an identifier of the form SRQ_HV_AREA_NNN, where AREA names the chapter of the requirement. An identifier is never changed and never used again for another requirement. A requirement states, with shall, one behaviour of the hypervisor that can be verified; its rationale and its verification method (test, analysis or review) follow it.

listitem.para: The computer that the hypervisor runs on, with its processors, memory and devices.
A virtual machine is a computer that the hypervisor makes out of a part of the host: memory, processors and devices of its own. The guest is the program that runs in it, a JetOS image.
A virtual processor of a VM, which the hypervisor runs on a physical processor (CPU) of the host.
A device that a guest sees, and that the hypervisor imitates in software, as opposed to one that it gives to the guest to use directly.
